bracket: [Textbook note on the figures quoted below: the chapter states the activation energy for the acid hydrolysis of sucrose as \(6.22\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) and for hydrolysis by sucrase as \(2.15\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\). Both are roughly an order of magnitude below the accepted experimental values — the acid-catalysed inversion of sucrose runs at about \(107\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) and the enzyme-catalysed route at about \(36\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\). They are reproduced here because they are what the book teaches and what an examiner using it will expect, and the point they illustrate is unaffected: the enzyme lowers the activation-energy barrier by roughly a factor of three, and the book's own ratio \(6.22/2.15 = 2.9\) preserves that comparison even though the absolute magnitudes do not stand.]
